title: Workspace Swivel: reconcile global sidebar, quick-switch, and route affordances
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: The current Console presents fragmented entry points for workspace switching (topbar chips, left rail workspace list, and command palette), inconsistent routing behaviour across deep-linked routes, and unclear affordances for route-scoped cost and rollout lenses. Users report friction when moving between workspaces while trying to keep dashboards and rollouts pinned to a context.

Goal: Produce an IA and interaction pattern set that unifies: 1) a single canonical workspace switch surface with progressive disclosure for recent/ favorite workspaces; 2) explicit route semantics so deep links preserve dashboard/rollout filter state; 3) left-rail ergonomics that support both global navigation (Projects, Models, Billing) and workspace-contextual quick-jump items; and 4) clear visual affordances for cost lenses and rollout pinned state.

Constraints: must reuse existing topbar real-estate where possible, avoid adding additional clicks for common flows (open dashboard -> view cost breakdown -> open rollout), and remain compatible with Dedicated/Private product variants where RBAC limits visibility.

Success metrics: decrease mean time-to-task for workspace switch + re-contextualize dashboards by 30% in prototype usability tests, 20% fewer support tickets about lost filters on deep links, and positive sentiment in NPS follow-ups for Console power users.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical switcher available via topbar and cmd-k with consistent recent/favorite ordering
Deep links maintain dashboard and rollout filters when ‘Pin context’ toggled
Left rail supports dual-mode: Global navigation vs Workspace quick-lane with clear visual separation
Prototype validated with 8 power users showing >30% improvement in switch-and-open-dashboard flow
Design handoff tokens and interaction specs delivered for engineering including edge-case flows (RBAC hidden items, >150 workspaces)
comments: 2026-02-14 - Aisha Patel: Initial sketch uploaded to Figma. Focused on two approaches: (A) topbar-centric canonical switcher + compact left rail, (B) rail-first persistent workspace lanes. Saved file: https://www.figma.com/file/abc123/workspace-swivel-v1

2026-02-20 - Jonah Rivera: Usability plan drafted. Recruiting 8 participants: 4 infra platform engineers, 2 growth PMs, 2 data scientists. Test script includes tasks: (1) switch workspace and open cost view, (2) deep-link to rollout and verify filter preservation, (3) re-pin dashboard to a workspace.

2026-02-25 - Design critique notes: PMs prefer approach A for new users; engineering favors B for predictable left-rail hot-paths. Trade-off: A is lower cognitive load for new users but requires more topbar overhead; B is denser and faster for power users.
2026-03-03 - Jonah Rivera: Prototype v0.2 posted. Live interactive prototype with pinned-context toggle and example deep links: https://www.figma.com/proto/abc123/workspace-swivel-v0.2

2026-03-05 - Research update: First 4 sessions completed. Initial findings: users expect workspace switch to be query-preserving when 'Pin context' is on; when off, they want a clean slate. Confusion arises when left-rail quick items look identical to global nav items. Need clearer visual separation (background vs border treatments).

2026-03-08 - PM feedback (Lina Morales): Include cost-lens affordance as a persistent crumb in the route bar (small chip) when cost-view is active so billing alerts can surface without losing workspace context. Also asked to include a keyboard shortcut map in onboarding modal.

2026-03-09 - Engineering (ENG-4982): Spike concluded showing feasibility for preserving query state across route transitions using router middleware. Performance note: serializing filter state into short tokens (max 384 chars) is required to avoid very long URLs. Linked PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/4982

2026-03-10 - Jonah Rivera: Submitted design for In Review. Attached detailed interaction flows and edge-case matrix. Next: handoff meeting with frontend on 2026-03-18 and accessibility audit scheduled for 2026-03-22.
notes: Avoid duplicating workspace lists between topbar and left rail — use progressive reveal for secondary actions
Consider a compact left-rail variant for screens <1280px where workspace quick-jump collapses to a chevron
Cost-lens chip should be read by screen readers and have an aria-label describing pinned filters
